name: Alternating Hammer Curl
research: Picture 1 left curled / right hanging, picture 2 reversed. Upper arms elev 10, plane 45 (a little wider than the palm-up curl so the back plate of the hanging dumbbell clears the thigh: fist ~0.30 m out from the midline, back plate edge x >= 0.21). Elbow 13 -> 124 (S1 range 123 +- 12). Neutral grip, axis kept square to the forearm in the forward-up plane: torso frame, du = (sin10 cos45, sin10 sin45, -cos10) = (0.123, 0.123, -0.985); hanging forearm (13 deg fold forward) = (0.117, 0.343, -0.933) -> axis forward minus its forearm part = (0, 0.94, 0.34) (thumb forward); curled forearm (124 deg) = (-0.081, 0.754, 0.652) -> thumb-up axis square to it = (0, -0.65, 0.76) (index toward the shoulder). Same numbers for the right hand (axis has no x, so the mirror is identical). S2 Kleiber 2015: biceps the same in neutral and supinated. Facts: research/alternating_hammer_curl.json.
